headline: INEOS-led Greensand opens EU's first full-scale offshore CO2 storage site
summary: King Frederik X opened Project Greensand at the Port of Esbjerg; the INEOS Energy / Harbour Energy / Nordsofonden venture moves into commercial operation, storing up to 400,000 t/yr of CO2 (initially from Danish biomethane plants) in the depleted Nini West field ~250 km offshore, with capacity designed to scale to 4-8 Mtpa.
co2crc_note: First operational EU full-scale offshore storage hub with cross-border intake and a biomethane-CO2 value chain - a live commercialisation template for CarbonNet/Bonaparte-style hubs.

headline: Worley completes FEED for INPEX's Abadi LNG and CCS infrastructure in Indonesia's Masela block
summary: Worley delivered front-end engineering design for two offshore packages - about 150 km of subsea infrastructure plus gas-export and CO2 pipelines - on INPEX's roughly US$21bn Abadi LNG project (9.5 Mtpa LNG) in the Masela block, a national strategic project that integrates CCS as it advances toward FID.
co2crc_note: Major APAC LNG-plus-CCS scheme advancing to FID; Indonesian storage and regulatory precedent is directly relevant to Australia-Asia CO2 value chains and CO2CRC regional engagement.
extractor_note: US$21bn is total project capex (not a discrete new commitment) - amount left null per golden rule.

headline: Vallourec wins tubular contract for Greece's Prinos CO2 storage project
summary: EnEarth (Energean) awarded Vallourec ~3,000 t of premium VAM casing pipe for phase one of the offshore Prinos CO2 store - an EU Project of Common Interest targeting up to 2.8 Mtpa injection (51.5 Mt total capacity). Vallourec separately took a >15,000 t line-pipe order for Petrobras' Sepia 2 development offshore Brazil.
co2crc_note: CCS supply chain maturing in Europe; Prinos is a depleted-oil-reservoir storage analogue relevant to Australian depleted-field storage economics.
extractor_note: Contract scope stated in tonnes of pipe, no monetary value disclosed - amount null.

headline: Japan Airlines and Climeworks sign world-first CORSIA-compliant carbon removal deal
summary: JAL agreed to buy carbon dioxide removal credits from Climeworks Solutions in what both describe as the first CORSIA-compliant CDR agreement - combining pathways such as soil carbon and biochar for the CORSIA-eligible portion, plus separate direct-air-capture credits - an early bridge of durable CDR into aviation compliance markets.
co2crc_note: Compliance-market (CORSIA) demand pulling durable CDR - a demand-side precedent relevant to Australia's CDR method development and Article 6 positioning.

headline: Public subsidy for Greensand CO2 storage draws scrutiny as INEOS defends state aid
summary: As Greensand opened, INEOS founder Jim Ratcliffe publicly defended the billions in state support underpinning Denmark's CO2 storage build-out, spotlighting the live social-licence and value-for-money debate around subsidised CCS infrastructure.
co2crc_note: Subsidy-justification and social-licence framing around a flagship storage hub - directly relevant to public-funding arguments for Australian CCS (Otway, CarbonNet).

headline: Asia-Pacific CCUS market could reach US$255bn by 2035, Xodus says
summary: Consultancy Xodus projected the APAC CCUS market could grow to around US$255bn by 2035, underscoring the region's investment pipeline across Australia, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia.
co2crc_note: APAC market-size signal supporting the investment case for Australian CCS capacity and CO2CRC's regional relevance.
extractor_note: US$255bn is a sector-wide market forecast (market-aggregate) - amount left null.
